This week I handed my newsletter to the one and only @queenofpeat, ecologist Merritt Turetsky. Her big idea? Stop treating wet land as a problem to drain. Start seeing it as something to work with instead!

🐸 What you can do: Become a bog champion: visit a local wetland and learn what lives there, ask your garden store to drop peat-based compost, and back the groups working to protect peatlands! For more, check out Merritt's new book, Bogland.

A new localized ceasefire negotiated by IAEA Director General @rafaelmgrossi took effect this morning to help prevent a nuclear accident in Ukraine during the military conflict. 

The eighth such IAEA-brokered temporary truce will enable repairs of equipment in a 330 kilovolt (kV) switchyard, close to the Zaporizhzhya Thermal Power Plant (ZTPP), that has been damaged by military activity. 

This will in turn strengthen the connection between the nearby Zaporizhzhya Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) and its sole remaining external power line, the Ferosplavna-1, and reduce the risk of another loss of off-site power. 

The ZNPP’s continued connection to the electrical grid is more important than ever as its fuel reserves for emergency diesel generators have been running low in recent months, weakening this last line of defence against a complete station blackout. 

Following demining, the repair work is expected to last several days, carried out on the frontline of the conflict and monitored by an IAEA team on the ground. 

DG Grossi says the Russian Federation and Ukraine engaged constructively with the IAEA to pave the way for the latest ceasefire, showing that persistent diplomatic efforts can yield concrete results that benefit both sides also in the most difficult and challenging of circumstances. 

The IAEA will continue its indispensable work to ensure nuclear safety and security during the conflict, DG Grossi says.

Today is probably a good time to check in on things with @privy_io, which became part of @stripe just over a year ago.

Our acquisition was predicated on three factors: stablecoin growth, self-custody as a key enabler of broader global coverage, and rapidly increasing demand for programmable financial infrastructure. As we said at the time, "money has to reside somewhere, and Privy builds the world's best programmable vaults."

Since then, the Privy team has executed exceptionally well: assets in Privy wallets have grown ~25x, monthly active developers are up ~3x, revenue is up ~9x, and Privy now facilitates nearly $25B of monthly transaction volume. @tryramp, @Deel, @Klarna, @felixpago, @HyperliquidX, and thousands of other businesses are building embedded banking functionality on Privy.

At Stripe, we're deeply integrating Privy into Treasury, @Link, and Connect. In each case, it's accelerating our global expansion, and enabling us to build better functionality faster. (Coming soon: @Link balances.)

We're also seeing that Privy's wallet infrastructure is the ideal substrate for agents to transact and earn -- live today with @merit_systems, @orthogonal_sh, @Nevermined_ai, @prlnet, and more. Developers prefer programmable financial infrastructure, but agents need it. We expect that the agentic economy will continue to grow extremely quickly.

The Privy team has maintained remarkable product velocity, with major launches this year including deposit addresses, earning on Privy balances, digital asset accounts, custodial wallets, and Stripe's own stablecoin cards.

It's also been neat to see how Privy has been accelerated by Stripe, with better onramps, @stablecoin payment rails and licenses, Stripe's fiat capabilities and issuing stack, and integration with @Tempo.

Together, we're building one API for holding stablecoin balances and earning yield, moving money in and out of fiat, and orchestrating spend with cards. We still have a lot of work to do, not least in integrating everything across Privy, Bridge, and the rest of Stripe -- there's been so much feature and functionality expansion that we haven't yet had much time to reconcile everything. Overall, though, I'm very happy with how things are going, and excited by where these capabilities are headed.

If you're interested in working on the future of stablecoins, agentic payments, and crypto's deployment in the real world, you should get in touch with @sternhenri (now leading all of @StripeCrypto) or others on the team.

A long-term perspective on humanity’s battle against malaria.

According to the latest data from the World Health Organization, the global death rate from malaria has almost halved since the year 2000.

The chart above puts this recent progress into a larger historical perspective. It combines the latest estimates from the WHO and the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation with those for the 20th century published by the late malaria researcher Richard Carter. Since 1900, the global death rate has declined by 96%. If it were still as high as it was then, around 16 million people would die from malaria every year instead of 610,000.

Behind this long-run decline is a shift in the distribution of the burden of malaria. In the first half of the 20th century, most malaria victims died in the Asian tropics. It was the substantial progress there — as well as in the Mediterranean and in the Americas — that made this vast improvement in human health possible.

Today, more than 9 out of 10 malaria deaths occur in Africa. This means that the recent progress shown in the chart is, above all, Africa’s progress.

(written by @MaxCRoser)

New work from Meta AI on agents that manage their own search.

(bookmark it)

A ReAct agent keeps every failed attempt in one context, making useful evidence harder to find.

To improve on this, they propose TreeFlex, a framework in which the agent’s own policy decides where to search.

On a deep-research benchmark, a 4B model reaches 48.8% versus 41.5% for flat ReAct, at the same context limit.

Is Bitcoin in trouble after Google's latest quantum computing breakthrough?

Short answer: not today. But the gap is getting smaller.

Google's new result makes one of the hardest parts of a quantum computer cheaper to build. That part is called "magic states."

Breaking Bitcoin's math needs a very large quantum computer, and these magic states are a big part of what makes it so large.

Google says the method still has to be shown at a larger scale.

In March, Google estimated the attack would need fewer than 500,000 physical qubits. Earlier estimates were in the millions.

A physical qubit makes errors all the time. To run a long program, hundreds of them are combined into one error-corrected "logical" qubit. Google's attack needs about 1,200 to 1,450 logical qubits, at roughly 400 physical qubits each.

Today, Google's Willow chip has 105 qubits. The biggest chip IBM has built has about 1,100. Even the biggest machines are roughly 450x too small.

The harder part is error correction. The most logical qubits reported so far is 96, by QuEra. The attack needs 13 to 15 times more.

IBM's roadmap targets 200 logical qubits by 2029 and 2,000 by 2033.

So if IBM hits its 2029 target, it would still be short of what the attack needs. Its 2033 target would be above it.

Google has already moved its own deadline to switch to quantum safe cryptography to 2029.

Bitcoin's proposed upgrade, BIP-360, has not been approved. Coinbase said on Oct 13 that an upgrade could take several years.

So Bitcoin is not in trouble today. No machine is close to doing this.

今儿看到携程CEO梁建章的一篇文章，大体是论如何通过补贴让出口人口维持住800万。

他给的药方：

（1）对每个孩子补贴累计至少20万。——动态根据GDP增加而上涨。

（2）一系列的制度：大力发展普惠托育服务，提高3岁以下婴幼儿的入托率；取消中考，淡化高考，减少教育内卷；适当缩短工作时长，有条件的企业推广灵活办公模式。同时，全社会还要倡导积极的婚育观，鼓励更多的年轻人结婚生育。

我觉得，这个招儿有意义，确实能让居民有实实在在的收获。

不过国内居民现在最大的问题，是对未来收入预期有着极高的不确定性。——这涉及到政策持续性、平衡性、经济变化、外贸、经济发展模式、外部条件变化等等诸多因素影响。

发钱固然能缓解一小会儿，但不能根治。诚然按照他的计算，假设每孩累计补贴总额为20万元，按照年出生人口1000万来计算，全国每年补贴总额为2万亿元，约占2025年GDP的1.4%。根据财政部发布的数据，2025年中国出口退税总额为2.13万亿元。即便全国每年育儿补贴总额达到2万亿元，还比不上出口退税总额多。

钱是不多，愿不愿意给是一码事，即便愿意那么其他地方呢？如果改不了照着老百姓这只羊往死里薅的路子，少薅两把解决不了太多的问题。——但我也支持给补贴，以高层的这点心思，别指望一次性榨出多少来。。。
